metadata.title: Agentic Dev Life Cycle.
metadata.note: Standalone teaching explainer (~2.5min) on the ADLC — the Agentic Development Life Cycle. FRAMEWORK-FIRST (built to pass PROOF): the reframe is shown before any example (B01: classic SDLC = you author; ADLC = you specify + verify, agent builds), then the loop (B02: specify→plan→build→verify→iterate, with owners), a worked example (B03: fixing a bug through the cycle), a falsifiability/edge case (B04: not fire-and-forget — skip spec or verify and it breaks), then a scaffolded task (B06). ONE insight: when agents write the code, your leverage moves to the two ends — specifying what 'done' means and verifying you got it; the gates are the point. Presented as a general pattern, not a single vendor's framework; no invented stats or product names (DOUBLE-CHECK LAW). Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro via Claude Remotion comps); body B01-B04 are house-style 4K PIL cards generated by make_cards.py.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. You know the software life cycle: plan, code, test, ship. But when an AI agent writes most of the code, that loop changes, and so does your job. This is the Agentic Development Life Cycle, and the surprise is what you end up doing in it.

props.command: What's the “agentic” development life cycle — and what's my job when the agent writes the code?

beats.narration_text: Here's the shift. In the classic cycle, you're the author, you plan it, you write it, you test it. In the agentic cycle, the agent writes it. Your job moves up a level: you specify what you want and what done means, and you verify what came back. You go from typing the code to directing and reviewing it.

card.title: Your Job Changes.
card.subtitle: author → director
card.caption: when the agent writes the code, your leverage moves up a level
card.footer: FROM WRITING CODE → TO DIRECTING + REVIEWING IT

beats.narration_text: So the loop looks like this. You specify, the intent, and the acceptance criteria. The agent plans. The agent builds, writing and running code in its own loop. Then you verify, review the diff, run the checks. And you iterate until it meets the criteria. Two steps are yours, two are the agent's.

show.event: the four phases light in order
the terracotta loop-back arrow closes the cycle

card.title: The Cycle.
card.subtitle: two steps yours, two the agent's
card.repeat_label: iterate — until it meets the acceptance criteria
card.caption: you own the two ends: say what “done” means, and check that you got it

beats.narration_text: Watch it on a bug. You specify: here's the bug, and done means these tests pass. The agent plans the fix, writes it, and runs the tests itself. You review the diff, catch one edge case, and send it back. It revises, tests pass, you merge. One cycle, with you at the two ends.

show.event: the bug + acceptance feed the cycle
the answer resolves: built, reviewed, merged (accent)

card.title: One Bug, One Cycle.
card.subtitle: you at the two ends
card.answer: agent plans → builds → tests → you review the diff → iterate once → merge
card.caption: you wrote the spec and the review; the agent wrote the code
card.footer: SPEC IN · VERIFY OUT · THE AGENT FILLS THE MIDDLE

beats.narration_text: Now the trap. This is not fire-and-forget. Skip the spec, and you get a confident answer to the wrong question. Skip the verify, and you're rubber-stamping slop, at machine speed. The agent amplifies whatever you give it, a sharp spec and a real review, or a vague one and no review. The gates are the point.

card.title: Not Fire-and-Forget.
card.subtitle: the gates are the point
card.caption: the agent amplifies whatever you give it — spec and review, or the lack of them
card.footer: NO SPEC = WRONG ANSWER · NO VERIFY = SLOP AT SCALE

beats.narration_text: So the agentic dev life cycle isn't about the agent doing everything. It's a loop, specify, plan, build, verify, iterate, where your leverage moves to the two ends: saying what good looks like, and checking that you got it.

props.artifactTitle: Agentic dev life cycle — one page
artifactLines: The loop: Specify → Plan → Build → Verify → Iterate — until it meets the acceptance criteria.
The agent owns Plan + Build; you own Specify + Verify — you direct and review, you don't type.
Specify = intent + what “done” means. Verify = review the diff and run the checks against it.
Not fire-and-forget: skip the spec and you solve the wrong problem; skip verify and you ship slop at scale.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take a task you'd normally just code yourself. Before you touch the keyboard, write down what done means, the acceptance criteria. Then let an agent build to it, and review only against that list. Notice how much of the real work was the spec and the review.

props.command: Take a task I'd normally code myself. Before any code: write what “done” means (acceptance criteria). Then build to it, and review only against that list.
output: let the agent build to them

beats.narration_text: The agentic dev life cycle. Specify, verify, iterate. Humanitarians AI.
